title: The Apple II most people used

summary.text: <u>[Apple //e](station:apple2e) joins as a second Apple II station, next to the 1988 GEOS desktop the museum already showed.</u> Almost nobody actually ran GEOS on an Apple II in the day, so this one boots the machine as it was really used: **ProDOS 8** brings up a one-keypress menu, the Apple II's own version of an `AUTOEXEC.BAT`, offering **AppleWorks**, the 80-column word processor, database and spreadsheet that made the //e a business machine, and **Dazzle Draw**, a double-hi-res paint program that pushed 16 colours out of hardware built for six. Both load in a couple of seconds from an emulated hard disk behind a CFFA card, and a keypress returns to the menu at any time. It runs host-native from day one, the same MAME driver family as the museum's Taiwanese MPF-II clone, with no bridge machine anywhere underneath it. A modern coda is planned too: a 2023 fan port of **Angry Birds** for the same 128 KB hardware, waiting only on a working copy of the disk image. [SAM Coupé](station:samcoupe) also joins the lineup, a 1989 British ZX Spectrum-compatible with far more machine behind it: a SAM BASIC boot menu offers **Manic Miner**, **Mr. Pac**, **Splat!** and **The Secretary**, a period word processor, all loaded from a single floppy disk image built to look period-authentic. It too is host-native MAME with no bridge underneath. [Atari 800XL](station:atari800xl) arrives too, host-native MAME, its **MyPicoDos** menu joystick-driven: **The Last Word**, **River Raid**, **Star Raiders**.

Safari 26 gained a native streaming write path: the gallery's video pipeline now offers `datagrams.createWritable()` alongside the older writable-stream fallback it already used everywhere else, so the newest Safari drives the same low-latency path Chrome and Firefox have had for months instead of falling back to a slower one. The walk-in cells used for signed-in visitors also picked up a shared client-debug plane, so a session that misbehaves on someone's own laptop can be inspected the same way a developer's own test session already could, without asking them to reproduce it twice.

The posters fact-checking pass kept going: two more period write-ups were checked line by line against primary sources, catching a wrong chip name and adding the Signetics 2513 character generator's own history — the chip that drew text on an early Apple II and, through a Philips/Signetics collaboration, on the BBC Micro's teletext decoder too. Thirteen of fifteen posters are now checked and merged.

<u>[Genode Sculpt OS](station:sculpt) joins as the museum's first microkernel desktop.</u> Genode Labs' Sculpt 25.04 turns the operating system itself into the interface: the **Leitzentrale** draws the running machine as a live graph of components, and every driver, service and application is a node the visitor can add, wire and inspect while it runs. The exhibit rests with the network up on the retronet and the **+** menu open on its Options, so toggling audio, a touchpad or the system clock grows the graph on screen. It runs under KVM with a relative USB mouse: Genode's HID driver never binds QEMU's absolute tablet, so the pointer is the museum's exact one-pixel-per-unit relative bridge, measured on the framebuffer.

bullets: [Apple //e](station:apple2e)'s STARTUP menu is a tokenized Applesoft program on the boot volume — the exact mechanism ProDOS used for an autoexec in 1985
Reset always returns [Apple //e](station:apple2e) to its menu: a MAME savestate captured there restores in half a second against a 2.6 second cold boot
An Apple II Mouse Card is wired into [Apple //e](station:apple2e) for Dazzle Draw, but its cursor does not yet track — the station ships keyboard-only until that is solved
[SAM Coupé](station:samcoupe)'s boot menu is a SAM BASIC program that loads from disk the moment SAMDOS finds it — the machine's own version of an autoexec
Reset always returns [SAM Coupé](station:samcoupe) to its menu: a savestate captured there restores in under two seconds
[Atari 800XL](station:atari800xl)'s boot menu is read straight off the joystick port, not a keyboard chord — the same arrow keys a visitor already has move the highlight
[Atari 800XL](station:atari800xl)'s savestate restores pixel-identical in 1.3s vs a 19-21s cold boot — measured, since the driver declares no save-state support

The 1985 Amiga 1000 and 1991 Amiga 3000 both moved onto FS-UAE's new host-native plane this week — shared-memory frames and a control socket instead of a virtual display, the same route the museum's MAME and VICE stations already use

The 1985 Amiga 1000 is dark-launched host-native on FS-UAE, booting Workbench 1.2 from floppy the way the real machine did — it had no Kickstart in ROM, only a write-control store loaded fresh from a Kickstart disk on every power-up

The Amiga 3000 fills the gap between Workbench 1.3 and 3.5 in the lineup: 1991's Workbench 2.04, host-native on the same FS-UAE path, sharing its Kickstart 2.04 A3000 ROM dump with the museum's Amiga UNIX station on the same hardware
